ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a set of triangular plates is placed as in Figure 1, with $AB=CD= \sqrt{6}$, and vertex $E$ coinciding. When $\triangle DEC$ is rotated around its vertex $E$, as in Figure 2, during the rotation, when $\angle AED=75^\circ$, and $AD$ and $BC$ are connected, what is the area of $\triangle ADE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 2, draw $EG \parallel CD$ through point E, extend CE to meet AB at point H, \\
$\therefore \angle EDC=\angle DEG$, \\
Given that, we know: $\angle EDC=30^\circ$, $\angle DEC=60^\circ$, $\angle ECD=\angle AEB=90^\circ$, $\angle ABE=\angle BAE=45^\circ$, \\
$\because \angle AED=75^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle AEG=\angle AED-\angle DEG=75^\circ-30^\circ=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore EG\parallel AB\parallel CD$, \\
$\therefore HC\perp AB$, \\
$\therefore HE=BH=AH=\frac{1}{2}AB$, \\
And since $AB=CD$, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram, \\
$\because AB=CD=\sqrt{6}$, \\
$\therefore HE=BH=AH=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$, EC=$\frac{CD}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{2}$, \\
HC=HE+EC=$\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}+\sqrt{2}=\frac{\sqrt{6}+2\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABE}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{6} \times \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{3}{2}$, $S_{\triangle DEC}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{6} \times \sqrt{2}=\sqrt{3}$, $S_{\triangle CEB}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, \\
$S_{\square ABCD}=\sqrt{6} \times \frac{\sqrt{6}+2\sqrt{2}}{2}=3+2\sqrt{3}$, \\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ADE}=S_{\square ABCD}-S_{\triangle ABE}-S_{\triangle DEC}-S_{\triangle CEB}=3+2\sqrt{3}-\frac{3}{2}-\sqrt{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\boxed{\frac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}}$.

When $\triangle DEC$ is rotated around its vertex $E$, as in Figure 2, during the rotation, when $\angle AED=75^\circ$, and $AD$ and $BC$ are connected, what is the area of $\triangle ADE$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in Figure 2, draw $EG \parallel CD$ through point E, extend CE to meet AB at point H, \\ $\therefore \angle EDC=\angle DEG$, \\ Given that, we know: $\angle EDC=30^\circ$, $\angle DEC=60^\circ$, $\angle ECD=\angle AEB=90^\circ$, $\angle ABE=\angle BAE=45^\circ$, \\ $\because \angle AED=75^\circ$, \\ $\therefore \angle AEG=\angle AED-\angle DEG=75^\circ-30^\circ=45^\circ$, \\ $\therefore EG\parallel AB\parallel CD$, \\ $\therefore HC\perp AB$, \\ $\therefore HE=BH=AH=\frac{1}{2}AB$, \\ And since $AB=CD$, \\ $\therefore$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram, \\ $\because AB=CD=\sqrt{6}$, \\ $\therefore HE=BH=AH=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$, EC=$\frac{CD}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{2}$, \\ HC=HE+EC=$\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}+\sqrt{2}=\frac{\sqrt{6}+2\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\ $\therefore S_{\triangle ABE}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{6} \times \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{3}{2}$, $S_{\triangle DEC}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{6} \times \sqrt{2}=\sqrt{3}$, $S_{\triangle CEB}=\frac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, \\ $S_{\square ABCD}=\sqrt{6} \times \frac{\sqrt{6}+2\sqrt{2}}{2}=3+2\sqrt{3}$, \\ $\therefore S_{\triangle ADE}=S_{\square ABCD}-S_{\triangle ABE}-S_{\triangle DEC}-S_{\triangle CEB}=3+2\sqrt{3}-\frac{3}{2}-\sqrt{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\boxed{\frac{3+\sqrt{3}}{2}}$
